$comment: Hand-maintained. Which rules apply in each mode (bin/build-rules.mjs adds `modes` to every rule in build/rules.json). Modes are nested: quick ⊂ client — every rule applies in client mode; a rule applies in quick mode when its id or prefix is listed under quick (ids win over prefixes; quickExclude removes ids from a listed prefix). The quick set is the SECURITY FLOOR, the THEME CORE (the 'Consistent' pillar: one token source, light + dark, contrast) and a lean build bar: nothing that protects secrets, identity, ownership, input, honesty or the agent itself is ever client-only. External obligations (stores, privacy law, public websites) are client-only because quick mode is only allowed while none of them applies (ENF-4). See ENGINEERING_STANDARD.md §0A. reviewedPointers: quick→client references checked by hand to be pointers (see-also, contrast, exemptions), not requirements; --check lists any new cross-mode reference and flags stale entries.

reviewedPointers.SEC-19>AI-9: pointer to §2D; only the quick AI-* rules apply in quick mode
reviewedPointers.AUTH-2>AUTH-4: condition: without enforced MFA (always so in quick) the 15-char minimum applies
reviewedPointers.AUTH-5>SLOG-1: context for 'accurate clocks', not a doc requirement
reviewedPointers.AI-4>API-4: contrast ('API-4 limits request rate'), not a requirement
reviewedPointers.PERF-3>API-7: PERF-3 restates the cursor requirement itself
reviewedPointers.LOG-3>REL-1: explains where error counts go once alerts exist (client)
reviewedPointers.LOG-4>LOG-1: names the field keys to keep; the schema itself is client-only
